texts.facts: The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 18.09.2022. 2. Due to the accidental injuries, he lost his income from the date of accident. The accidental injuries have caused permanent disability to the petitioner. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EU-6099 and the Magadi Police have registered a case in Cr.No.0303/2023 for offences p/u/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC. The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 4. In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, placed ex-parte.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions: (i) ILR 204 Kar 3336 : Branch Manager, Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt. Kempamma And Ors. Nagesh D.M vs Premasagar M.K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96429739/ 3 (ii) ILR 2009 kar 2921 : Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. B.C.Kumar and Anr. (iii) ILR 2021 Kar 146 : The Divisional Manager, United India Ins. Co. Ltd., Belagavi Vs. Smt. Reshma and Ors. (iv) ILR 2010 Kar 2439 : Sri. Subash Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Rep. by its Manager and Ors. 9. The Respondent No.2 has contended that there is no loss of income due to the injuries being suffered by the petitioner and has relied on the admission by PW.1 that his income is the same as before. But before giving such an admission PW.1 has stated he works under a Contractor, he is unable to lift load but he does other Electrical work. This shows that the disability is coming in the way of his regular work. The income may remain same due to the nature of the work of the petitioner being manual work. There will not be considerable change in the income of laborers within a few years. But, the disability suffered by him will always affect his efficiency in work. As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,57,120/-. The Petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 12% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions: (i) ILR 204 Kar 3336 : Branch Manager, Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt. Kempamma And Ors. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the case was shown as a self fall and the claimants built up a case that the deceased was a pillion rider only to get compensation and the petition was not maintainable. However the respondent No.2 has failed to prove its defence of fraud by the petitioner. Therefore, the Respondents being the Owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 18.09.2022 at 6.30 to 7.00pm, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EU- 6099 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3. What order or award?

It has also got examined its official/Asst. Manager Mr.Pradeep K.S. as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
8.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASON

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EU-6099 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P.1
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
The Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the offending motorcycle in the accident.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself and he sustained grievous injuries by not wearing helmet.

In the cross- examination of PW.1, he has stated that he did not have DL.
11.
In support of the defence the respondent No.2 has got examined Dr.Nagaraja Upadhya - Medical Officer as RW.1.
He has deposed in his chief examination that, there is no MLC register extract and police intimation was sent in the name of the petitioner.
He has given preliminary first aid treatment to the petitioner.
They did not register the MLC in this case since the petitioner took only first aid.
The petitioner gave the history as fall from bike.
They have given OPD slip for first aid treatment.
During the cross examination of RW.1, he has stated that on 18.09.2022 the petitioner has taken first aid treatment in their hospital.

12. The documents at Exs.P.1 to P.8 i.e., FIR with Complaint, PF, spot mahazar, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet are in accordance with the statement given

No contrary evidence is led against these documents from the side of respondent No.2.
13.
As per Ex.P.7/Wound Certificate, the petitioner sustained injuries on 18.09.2022 in an RTA.
This shows that on account of the accident the Petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
Therefore, on overall perusal of Exs.P.1 to 8 it is clear that the accident occurred on 18.09.2022 and the petitioner sustained injuries as mentioned in Ex.P.7.

The point of dispute between the parties is Nagesh D.M vs Premasagar M.K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96429739/
4 the status of the petitioner in the bike i.e., whether he was the rider or the pillion rid
In order to buttress their contention the respondent No.2 has relied on the oral evidence of RW.1/Medical Officer of Mytri Hospital.
But no supporting document is produced.
Therefore, this contention cannot be accepted.
The respondent No.2 has also contended that there is 12 days delay in registering the FIR and the petitioner has cooked up a story showing him as the pillion rider.

But it is to be noted here that the petitioner got admitted to Mythri Hospital as per RW.1 for first aid treatment on 18.09.2022 and later went to Vijayanagara Hospital on 21.09.2022 and the FIR was registered on 30.09.2022.
Such being the case, it is clear that the accident in fact occurred and the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident.
Only the fact of delay in registering the FIR cannot be held against the petitioner.
As such, on perusal of the above said documents this Tribunal holds that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the Petitioner has suffered (i) Fracture of right olecranon bone and (ii) Abrasion over right foot.
Out of these injuries, injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

15. The petitioner has got examined Mr.Naveen Kumar T.B. - Medical Record Incharge as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 to P.16 authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register extract and case sheet with X-ray.
During the cross examination of PW.2, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
16. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as per PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.17 & 18 i.e., Clinical notes and X-ray.
In the cross examination of PW.3, he has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has not taken opinion form the treated Doctor.
Further admitted that the shoulder and wrists ROM and Power are normal and the ROM at the elbow is not severe.
Fractures are united, implants are in situ.
After removal of implants the present complaints may vary.
17. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was working as an Electrician and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
From the evidence of PW.3 it can be seen that the petitioner is suffering total disability of the right Arm at 37% and to the whole body at 12%, which will impact his work and efficiency.
In the evidence of PW.3, he has stated that the petitioner can do Desk Jobs.
However the petitioner as an Electrician has to fold his hand and movements of hand is there.
Due to this disability the petitioner cannot do his work easily.
Therefore, the court deems it fit to consider the Functional disability at 12%.

Monthly income:
18.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Electrician work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank Statement, vouchers, receipts etc., to quantify the income.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.

Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Nagesh D.M vs Premasagar M.K on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96429739/
5 Rs.15,500/- per month.
19.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 33 years as could be made out from Ex.P.9/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Mythri Hospital, Magadi wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Vijayanagar Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 21.09.2022 to 24.0
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary of Vijayanagar hospital.
Considering the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.14 for a sum of Rs.1,16,724/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for in the above said Hospitals which can be made out from Ex.P.10 Discharge summary.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 4 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implant, the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.3 have not produced any estimation letter.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.1,16,724/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,500/- period Nagesh D.M vs Premasagar M.K on 10 December, 202

Loss of future income Rs.3,57,120/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7.

Future Medical Expenses Rs.40,000/-
TOTAL Rs.6,29,344/-

If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.6,29,500/-
and same is awarded to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 21.
The respondent No.2 has got examined Mr.Pradeep K.S. - assistant Manager as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 authorization letter and copy of policy.

During the cross examination of RW.2,
he has admitted that the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
The petitioner was a pillion rider.
Further admitted that the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the motorcycle and it is wrongly filed.
They have not produced any MLC register extract to show self fall from bike.
To prove the same the respondents did not produce any documents.
(ii) ILR 2009 Kar 2921 : Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. B.C.Kumar and Anr.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that 'Plea of guilt by the driver cannot become the sole criterion for allowing the claim petition by the MACT'.
(iii) ILR 2021 Kar 146 : The Divisional Manager, United India Ins. Co. Ltd., B
Though the petitioner has claimed Rs.30,00,000/- but, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.6,29,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
22. Issue No.3:

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,29,500/- (Rupees Six  Lakhs Twenty Nine Thousand and Five Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. (Except future medical expenses) from the date of petition ti
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
